name: Implicit Stereotypes
description: Group cues can automatically activate stereotype-linked traits or expectations before a person consciously endorses, rejects, or corrects them. This is narrower than stereotyping in general: it is specifically about fast, often involuntary category-trait activation.
design_relevance_note: Highly relevant to inclusive design, moderation, ranking, hiring/internal tools, synthetic-persona work, and model evaluation, where automatic group-trait associations can leak into interpretation or downstream decisions. Its relevance is strongest in fairness-sensitive domains rather than everyday layout or interaction design.
prevalence_note: Well known inside fairness, inclusive-design, and responsible-AI conversations, often under the broader umbrella of implicit bias, but still relatively specialized outside those contexts.

findings.description: Devine's studies found that cultural stereotype content can be activated automatically by group-related primes and shape judgments of ambiguous behavior even when individuals differ in explicit prejudice and later controlled correction.
findings.source_title: Stereotypes and prejudice: Their automatic and controlled components.
findings.source_venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
